prompt.context_jp: 給湯室の脇のゴミ箱を覗き込んだ千葉小夏の目に、明らかに家庭ゴミと分かる袋___飛び込んでくる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 袋___飛び込んでくる
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits: a bag ___ catches her eye.

feedback.correct_en: The bag is brand-new information suddenly entering Konatsu's field of vision — a classic 'something appears' moment that takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the bag an already-established topic, which clashes with the surprise. を doesn't fit with the intransitive 飛び込んでくる.

contrast_examples.jp: 目に光が飛び込んできた。
contrast_examples.en: A light caught my eye. (new sight → が)

contrast_examples.jp: その袋は家庭ゴミだった。
contrast_examples.en: That bag (which we were just discussing) was household waste. (topic → は)

prompt.context_jp: ゴミ袋を指差した女の声に___、一切の遠慮がなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 女の声に___、一切の遠慮がなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits.

feedback.correct_en: に+は marks 'as for that voice' — setting the voice as the topic whose characteristic (no hesitation) is then described.
feedback.incorrect_en: が after に is ungrammatical here; を doesn't match the stative 'なかった'.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の声には力があった。
contrast_examples.en: His voice had power. (topic-marking には)
A voice was audible. (new event → が)

prompt.context_jp: フロアの空気___、瞬時に凍りついた。
prompt.prompt_jp: フロアの空気___、瞬時に凍りついた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: This is an eventive, scene-painting sentence — the floor's atmosphere is newly introduced as it 'freezes'. New-information が is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn it into a generic topic statement, losing the sudden, dramatic feel. に is wrong grammatically.

contrast_examples.en: The air froze. (event report → が)
The atmosphere is heavy. (general description → は)

prompt.context_jp: 「会社___あなたの家ではありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 会社___あなたの家ではありません
prompt.prompt_en: Omae tells Ide about work vs home.

feedback.correct_en: This is a definitional/categorical statement about 'the company' as topic: what it IS and ISN'T. は is the natural topic marker for 'A は B ではありません'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would wrongly treat 'company' as new info in an identifying frame. も (also) makes no sense here.

contrast_examples.en: This place is a company. (topic は)
There is a company. (existence → が)

prompt.context_jp: 「たかが ゴミの1つや2つで 派遣___社員をパワハラするな！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 派遣___社員をパワハラするな
prompt.prompt_en: The manager yells at Omae.

feedback.correct_en: Here 派遣 is the subject of パワハラする in a specific, newly-introduced accusation. が picks out 'a temp' as the actor — almost exhaustive-listing: 'of all people, a TEMP harassing an employee!'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'temps' a general topic and weaken the indignant, pointed accusation. に is wrong grammatically.

contrast_examples.jp: 派遣が社員に意見した。
contrast_examples.en: A temp gave an employee their opinion. (specific actor → が)
Temps (in general) are in a weak position. (topic → は)

prompt.context_jp: 「うちの新入社員の教育___ 我々 社員の役目だ」
prompt.prompt_jp: うちの新入社員の教育___ 我々 社員の役目だ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 'Training our new hires' is the topic being defined: 'as for X, it's our job.' This 'A は B だ' structure uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly assert new information. を can't attach to the subject of the equative sentence.

contrast_examples.jp: 教育は社員の役目です。
contrast_examples.en: Training is the employees' role. (topic → は)
Training is needed. (focus on need → が)

prompt.context_jp: 「今 やってる作業 大前さん___いないとできません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 大前さん___いないとできません
prompt.prompt_en: 'I can't do this work without Omae.'

feedback.correct_en: Inside a 〜と conditional clause, the subject typically takes が, not は. Also, it exhaustively identifies Omae as the specific missing person.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside an embedded 'if not there' clause sounds unnatural; it tends to float out as a contrastive topic. に would mark a location/target, not the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 社長がいないと会議ができない。
contrast_examples.en: We can't have the meeting if the CEO isn't here. (が in conditional)
The CEO is never around. (main-clause topic は)

prompt.context_jp: 今や 派遣なしに 会社___回らない
prompt.prompt_jp: 会社___回らない
prompt.prompt_en: 'Companies can't run without temps.'

feedback.correct_en: This is a generic, aphoristic statement — 'companies (as a category)' is the topic. は fits the general-truth tone of the narration.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight a particular company as new info, breaking the generalizing tone. を can't mark the subject of 回らない.

contrast_examples.en: Companies run on people. (generic → は)
The company went bankrupt. (specific event → が)

prompt.context_jp: 彼女の辞書に "不可能"と"残業"の文字___ない
prompt.prompt_jp: "不可能"と"残業"の文字___ない
prompt.prompt_en: 'The words impossible and overtime do not exist.'

feedback.correct_en: Negative existence with contrastive emphasis: 'as for those words, they don't exist (unlike other words).' は highlights the contrast and is standard with ない.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just report absence neutrally and weakens the rhetorical punch. も would mean 'also don't exist', which isn't the meaning.

contrast_examples.en: There's no time (as for time). (contrastive は)
No time! (neutral report → が)

prompt.context_jp: 「社員と派遣___ 全く同じ待遇になったら…」
prompt.prompt_jp: 社員と派遣___ 全く同じ待遇になったら
prompt.prompt_en: 'If employees and temps become treated exactly the same...'

feedback.correct_en: Inside a conditional clause (〜たら), the subject typically takes が. This introduces the hypothetical new situation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a 〜たら clause sounds unnatural and reads as a contrastive topic jumping out of the clause. を can't mark the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降ったら中止です。
contrast_examples.en: If it rains, it's canceled. (が in たら-clause)
I don't like rain. (main-clause topic は)

prompt.context_jp: 井手の顔___血の気が引いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 井手の顔___血の気が引いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'Ide's face drained of color.'

feedback.correct_en: 血の気が引く takes から on the source — color drained FROM his face. The subject slot is already filled by 血の気が.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would create a double subject with no coherent reading. を is wrong since 引く here is intransitive 'recede'.

contrast_examples.en: Sweat flowed from his face. (source → から)
His face turned red. (subject → が)

prompt.context_jp: 「これ___ シュレッダーにかけて 破棄すべき内部書類です」
prompt.prompt_jp: これ___ シュレッダーにかけて 破棄すべき内部書類です
prompt.prompt_en: Omae identifies the document.

feedback.correct_en: Classic 'A は B です' identifying sentence: 'As for this, it's an internal document.' Topic は is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight 'this one (among others) is the document', which doesn't match the explanatory tone.

contrast_examples.en: This is a confidential document. (identifying は)

contrast_examples.jp: これが問題の書類です。
contrast_examples.en: THIS is the document in question. (exhaustive が)

prompt.context_jp: フロアの奥から、宇野部長の怒声___飛んできた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 宇野部長の怒声___飛んできた
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'Manager Uno's angry voice came flying.'

feedback.correct_en: An event-report: a shout suddenly comes flying across the floor — a prototypical new-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn his shout into a pre-existing topic, killing the surprise. に marks a target, not the subject.

contrast_examples.en: A voice flew over. (new event → が)
The voice (that we were talking about) carried well. (topic は)

prompt.context_jp: 「新入社員の教育___ 社員の役目 派遣は口を出すな」
prompt.prompt_jp: 新入社員の教育___ 社員の役目
prompt.prompt_en: The manager asserts whose job training is.

feedback.correct_en: 'As for training new hires, (it's) the employees' job' — a definitional topic statement, contrasting with what follows about temps (派遣は). は matches the parallel contrastive frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly spotlight 'training' as new. も (also) doesn't fit the exclusive claim.

contrast_examples.jp: 教育は社員、雑務は派遣。
contrast_examples.en: Training is for employees; chores are for temps. (parallel contrastive は)
Training is lacking. (new info → が)

prompt.context_jp: 「井手___な "テイスト･オブ･ライフ"の 御曹司なんだ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 井手___な "テイスト･オブ･ライフ"の 御曹司なんだ
prompt.prompt_en: The boss reveals who Ide really is.

feedback.correct_en: 'As for Ide, he's the heir to Taste of Life' — a topic-and-comment identification. The な is the colloquial filler attached to topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mean 'IDE (of all people) is the heir', which reverses the information flow; the audience already knows who Ide is.

contrast_examples.en: Ide is an heir. (describing known person → は)
It's Ide who is the heir. (identifying among candidates → が)

prompt.context_jp: 「あいつ___ テイスト･オブ･ライフの 創業者の女社長の三男坊だ」
prompt.prompt_jp: あいつ___ 三男坊だ
prompt.prompt_en: 'That guy is the third son of the female founder.'

feedback.correct_en: Topic-comment: 'As for that guy, (he) is the third son...' は fits the explanatory, introducing-info-about-a-known-person tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would emphasize that HE (as opposed to someone else) is the third son — not the point here.

contrast_examples.en: He is (her) son. (description of known entity)
HE is the son (not the others). (identifying が)

prompt.context_jp: 「わが会社人生 最大 最速の 追い風___吹いて来た」
prompt.prompt_jp: 追い風___吹いて来た
prompt.prompt_en: Tokairin feels a tailwind coming.

feedback.correct_en: A tailwind is being newly perceived/announced as appearing — classic が for a new-event subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'the tailwind' an already-established topic, which doesn't match the excited discovery tone.

contrast_examples.en: The wind started blowing. (new event → が)
A tailwind is welcome (in general). (generic → は)

prompt.context_jp: 「賢ちゃん___勝ちだ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 賢ちゃん___勝ちだ
prompt.prompt_en: 'Ken wins (the bet).'

feedback.correct_en: 賢ちゃんの勝ち = 'Ken's win' — the noun phrase takes possessive の. Tokairin is declaring whose victory it is.
feedback.incorrect_en: は or が would treat 賢ちゃん as a clause-level subject, but 勝ちだ here is a nominal predicate whose possessor is Ken.

contrast_examples.en: It's your win. (possessive の)
You won. (verbal, subject が)

prompt.context_jp: 「そんなもの___幻想です」
prompt.prompt_jp: そんなもの___幻想です
prompt.prompt_en: Omae on 'equal pay for equal work'.

feedback.correct_en: 'As for such a thing, it's an illusion' — dismissive topic-comment judgment. は fits the sweeping declarative tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly single out one thing as THE illusion among others. に is wrong grammatically.

contrast_examples.en: That's a lie. (dismissive topic は)
THAT is the truth. (identifying が)

prompt.context_jp: 小夏が___ても、彼女は袋を手に取ってフロアの中央へ歩き出す。
prompt.prompt_jp: 小夏が___ても
prompt.prompt_en: Konatsu tries to stop Aki from making a scene.

feedback.correct_en: 引き留める = hold someone back / dissuade them from leaving or acting. Fits Konatsu trying to stop Aki.
feedback.incorrect_en: 引き出す = pull out/withdraw (money, info). 引き受ける = take on (a task). Neither matches 'hold back a person'.

contrast_examples.en: I held my colleague back.
I withdrew money.

prompt.context_jp: 「___ では今後 新入社員には 一切 関わりません」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ では今後 新入社員には 一切 関わりません
prompt.prompt_en: Omae's polite acceptance of the boss's order.

feedback.correct_en: 承知しました is the formal business acknowledgment Omae uses — appropriately crisp and polite toward a superior.
feedback.incorrect_en: 了解です is casual/peer-level and considered impolite upward. 分かった is plain-form, far too casual for this workplace confrontation.

contrast_examples.jp: 承知しました、すぐに手配します。
contrast_examples.en: Understood, I'll arrange it right away. (business polite)
Got it, I'll do it later. (casual peer)

prompt.context_jp: 「これ ___で データ まとめといて」
prompt.prompt_jp: これ ___で データ まとめといて
prompt.prompt_en: Kadota's constant rush order to temps.

feedback.correct_en: なるはや = 'なるべく早く' (ASAP). It's the recurring buzzword the employees keep flinging at the temps.
feedback.incorrect_en: のんびり (leisurely) and そのうち (sometime) would signal the opposite — no urgency — which clashes with the demanding tone.

contrast_examples.en: Submit it ASAP.
I'll contact you sometime.

prompt.context_jp: 「一般的に 逆さまに押した場合 "___ 承認した"という ニュアンスを含みます」
prompt.prompt_jp: "___ 承認した"
prompt.prompt_en: The nuance of an upside-down stamp.

feedback.correct_en: 渋々 = reluctantly. An inverted hanko signals reluctant approval — this is the exact nuance Omae explains.
feedback.incorrect_en: 喜んで (gladly) is the opposite feeling; 直ちに (immediately) is about speed, not willingness.

contrast_examples.en: I reluctantly accepted.
I gladly accepted.

prompt.context_jp: 「あんな お時給モンスターにさ 時間___暇なんかないから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 時間___暇なんかないから
prompt.prompt_en: Tokairin refuses to spend time on Omae.

feedback.correct_en: 時間を割く is the fixed collocation 'to spare/devote time'. Tokairin says he has no time to spare for her.
feedback.incorrect_en: 時間を切る/抜く aren't natural collocations for 'spare time'. 切る evokes cutting off; 抜く evokes skipping.

contrast_examples.jp: 時間を割いてくれてありがとう。
contrast_examples.en: Thanks for sparing the time.
To cut corners.

prompt.context_jp: 「商品よりも前に まずは おのれを___意気込みで行け」
prompt.prompt_jp: おのれを___意気込みで行け
prompt.prompt_en: Uno's sales pep talk.

feedback.correct_en: 自分を売り込む = pitch/sell oneself (to a client). Standard sales idiom and the exact meaning intended.
feedback.incorrect_en: 売り切る = sell out (completely). 売り出す = put on sale / launch (a product). Neither fits 'promote yourself'.

contrast_examples.en: Pitch yourself.
Launch a new product.

prompt.context_jp: 「___ お渡ししたサンプルの パッケージの裏を 確認いただけますでしょうか」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ お渡ししたサンプルの…確認いただけますでしょうか
prompt.prompt_en: Mita apologizes on the phone to a client.

feedback.correct_en: 大変恐れ入りますが is the formal cushion phrase for making a troublesome request of a customer. Matches the apologetic business tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 悪いんだけど / ちょっといい？ are casual and would be rude to a client on a recall call.

contrast_examples.jp: 恐れ入りますが、ご確認ください。
contrast_examples.en: I'm sorry to trouble you, but please confirm. (business polite)
Sorry, but check it. (casual peer)

prompt.context_jp: 「派遣は 自分の仕事が___ なんぼ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の仕事が___ なんぼ
prompt.prompt_en: Omae's philosophy for temp workers.

feedback.correct_en: 〜てなんぼ is an idiom meaning 'only worth anything when you can 〜'. Omae says a temp is only worth it when they can do their own work.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見てなんぼ/聞いてなんぼ don't cohere with the sense of professional competence Omae is asserting.

contrast_examples.jp: 営業は数字を出してなんぼだ。
contrast_examples.en: Sales is only worthwhile when you deliver numbers.

contrast_examples.jp: 芸人は笑わせてなんぼ。
contrast_examples.en: A comedian is only worth it when they make people laugh.

prompt.context_jp: Omae scolds Ide for bringing home trash to the office.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as a sharp workplace rebuke?

choices.text: 会社はあなたの家ではありません。
会社があなたの家じゃないです。
あなたの家は会社ではありません。

feedback.correct_en: Topic は + ではありません gives a crisp, formal, definitional rebuke — exactly Omae's register.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses が, which oddly spotlights 'company' as new info, and じゃないです is softer/less sharp. C reverses the topic and ends up saying 'your home is not a company', which isn't the point.

contrast_examples.jp: ここは職場です、遊び場ではありません。
contrast_examples.en: This is a workplace, not a playground.
THIS is the workplace. (identifying が)

prompt.context_jp: Omae replies calmly to the shouting manager.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural as Omae's deadpan business pushback?

choices.text: 業務上 最小限のミスを指摘したまでですが、何か？
仕事でちょっとミスを言っただけだけど、何？
業務のミスを指摘しただけなので、何かありますか？

feedback.correct_en: 〜たまでですが、何か？ is a cool, slightly cutting business idiom meaning 'I merely pointed out X — got a problem?' Matches Omae's trademark tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is casual and loses the icy polish. C is grammatically fine but flabby and lacks the bite of 〜たまでです.

contrast_examples.jp: 事実を述べたまでです。
contrast_examples.en: I merely stated the facts.
I just said the facts. (plain, less elegant)

prompt.context_jp: Omae at 5pm sharp, telling the manager to move.
prompt.prompt_en: Which variant best captures Omae's blunt punch-out line?

choices.text: 邪魔です。定時なので失礼します。
ちょっと邪魔なんですけど、もう帰ってもいいですか？
すみません、お時間なのでお先に。

feedback.correct_en: Short, flat, 定時なので失礼します — bluntly polite. Captures Omae's famous 'punch-out-exactly-on-time' personality.
feedback.incorrect_en: B softens with ちょっと and asks permission, which Omae never does. C is too deferential and apologetic for her character.

contrast_examples.jp: 定時なので失礼します。
contrast_examples.en: It's quitting time, so I'm off. (crisp)

contrast_examples.jp: すみません、お先に失礼します。
contrast_examples.en: Excuse me, I'll head out first. (deferential)

prompt.context_jp: Omae confronts Ide about the document in the recycle bin.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural as a cool, accusatory confirmation?

choices.text: この書類を資源ゴミに捨てたのは、あなたですね？
あなたはこの書類を資源ゴミに捨てましたか？
この書類が資源ゴミに捨てられたのは、あなたですね？

feedback.correct_en: The cleft 〜のは、あなたですね？ puts the spotlight on 'you' as the identified actor — a classic calm, pinning-down accusation.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is a neutral yes/no question — flat, no bite. C's passive is clunky and buries who did it.

contrast_examples.en: The one who did it was you, right? (cleft, pinpoints)
Did you do it? (neutral question)

prompt.context_jp: Omae realizes they are locked inside the cold storage.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as a flat, resigned report of the situation?

choices.text: 閉じ込められちゃいました。
閉じ込められてしまっている状態です。

feedback.correct_en: Plain 〜ました passive is clipped and deadpan — matches Omae's unflappable 'just stating a fact' delivery.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 〜ちゃいました adds a rueful/colloquial note that doesn't fit Omae. C is over-explanatory and stiff.

contrast_examples.en: We've been locked in. (flat report)

contrast_examples.jp: 鍵をかけられちゃいました。
contrast_examples.en: Oops, we got locked in. (rueful tone)
